name: Acleisanthes

project_scope.selection_mode: Two approved source-pool taxa; both canonical species already installed in live manifest.
project_scope.source_pool: Master Plant Pool rows 15–16; Genus Study Index row 132
project_scope.species_installation: both installed and verified in data/manifest.json on 2026-10-15; genus lesson only; no species edits

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Inspect a fully opened flower SIDEWAYS and measure its narrow perianth tube. Acleisanthes longiflora can have a remarkably long 7–17 cm tube; A. obtusa has a much shorter open perianth around 2.5–5.5 cm total. Then find mature anthocarps and inspect ridges and hairs. Check both ordinary open (chasmogamous) and closed, self-pollinating (cleistogamous) flowers.
shared_traits: Dry-country Nyctaginaceae herbs or small subshrubs with mostly opposite, unequal paired simple leaves; a petaloid fused perianth WITHOUT a separate true corolla.
Flowers may be open and conspicuous or reduced and self-pollinating, so a plant can fruit without any large obvious trumpet being seen.
Fruits are 1-seeded anthocarps — the persistent perianth base encloses the fruit; ribs/ridges, grooves and capitate or beadlike hairs matter.
shared_genus_recognition.anatomy_warning: What looks like a corolla is the petaloid perianth; the species ID depends on tube and anthocarp, not 'number of petals'.

species_comparison_matrix.A. longiflora: Perianth tube exceptionally long, ca. 7–17 cm × 1–2 mm; limb 10–20 mm across
species_comparison_matrix.A. obtusa: Open perianth overall ca. 2.5–5.5 cm long; limb 13–25 mm across; tube 1–2 mm diameter

species_comparison_matrix.A. longiflora: Lanceolate to linear-lanceolate or triangular-lanceolate, often narrow with cuneate/decurrent base
species_comparison_matrix.A. obtusa: Usually deltate to broadly deltate-ovate, truncate to round or subcordate base

species_comparison_matrix.A. longiflora: Often undulate/crispate margin, apex acute/acuminate or long-attenuate
species_comparison_matrix.A. obtusa: Usually flat to slightly wavy margin, broad-round or acute and often apiculate tip

species_comparison_matrix.weight: OVERLAPPING: do not use length alone

species_comparison_matrix.A. longiflora: Five thin often hyaline/transparent longitudinal ridges and paired shallow grooves; glands lacking
species_comparison_matrix.A. obtusa: Five ribs plus paired deeper grooves, each rib/groove pair ending in a small inconspicuous glandless knob

species_comparison_matrix.A. longiflora: Ascending to trailing branched perennial, usually solitary open flowers, rare paired flowers
species_comparison_matrix.A. obtusa: Low spreading or prostrate branched plant, solitary flowers or 2–5-flowered cymes

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: fully expanded open chasmogamous flower with entire tube and ruler
look_here_first_sequence.if: tube 7 cm or longer, very narrow
look_here_first_sequence.then: Strongly favors A. longiflora. Confirm narrow wedge-based leaves and anthocarp ridges.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: open flower of much shorter 2.5–5.5 cm total length plus broad leaves
look_here_first_sequence.if: broad delta-shaped leaves with truncate/rounded base
look_here_first_sequence.then: Favors A. obtusa; confirm rib-and-knob pattern on mature anthocarp.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: mature anthocarp side and top with macro
look_here_first_sequence.if: thin translucent ridges versus prominent rib/groove ends with tiny knobs
look_here_first_sequence.then: Use as reproductive confirmation, especially if open flowers unavailable.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: fruit-bearing plant with no showy trumpet
look_here_first_sequence.then: Check for cleistogamy in both species; do not assume absent large flowers means different genus.
Use Acleisanthes sp. pending tube or mature anthocarp rather than guessing from white flowers

scientific_cautions: Both species can make small cleistogamous flowers; their size is not the same as the large open flower used in the first comparison row.
Flower tube length applies to OPEN chasmogamous flowers and must be measured from the base through the narrow tube, not just the flaring limb.
Fruit sizes overlap (6–8 mm); ridges, grooves and indumentum need high-resolution matched macros.
Perianth versus corolla terminology matters; do not label the visible tube as a fused true corolla.
A. obtusa is accepted by POWO with A. berlandieri and A. greggii as synonyms; these are not separate new lesson species.
Both Acleisanthes species are installed canonical learners. Admission does not imply a new native-range decision.

local_lookalike_routing.separator: Look for bract/involucre arrangement and anthocarp ribs, plus Acleisanthes very long flower tube in longiflora.
Usually much smaller clustered flowers with strongly ribbed/glandular anthocarps; focus on flower organization and fruit hair/glands.
Clustered showy magenta flower arrangement and distinctive anthocarp; compare flower clusters and fruit rather than color.
Morning-glories have a true corolla plus distinct calyx and different fruit; Acleisanthes has single petaloid perianth and anthocarp.

diagnostic_photo_requirements.show: complete narrow tube from base to limb, centimeter ruler and labels, 7–17 cm vs 2.5–5.5 cm
opposite unequal pair, cuneate/decurrent longiflora vs truncate/rounded obtusa base, petiole and margin
5 anthocarp ribs, intercostal grooves, summit knobs/hyaline ridges, 5–10 mm scale
chasmogamous versus cleistogamous flowers on real plants; do not misread small closed flowers as species ID
capitate hairs, moniliform hairs, ridges and groove surfaces at same magnification

diagnostic_photo_requirements.role: whole flowering habit and flower arrangement
diagnostic_photo_requirements.show: one or several flowers, foliage form and variable trailing branches; support only

dependencies.detail: Both species already appear in canonical manifest; do not duplicate installs. Genus-level photo and comparison improvements only.
Prioritize exact-species open flower tube with ruler, matched ripe anthocarps and closed-vs-open flower distinction. Retain creator/license/source link and annotation provenance.
Keep A. berlandieri and A. greggii aliases routed to accepted A. obtusa; clarify difficult mature anthocarp identifications without inventing exact gland thresholds.

comparison_cards.title: The trumpet-length split
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Measure the whole open flower correctly: longiflora's tube about 7–17 cm; obtusa's open perianth 2.5–5.5 cm overall.
comparison_cards.caution: Do not compare a closed self-pollinating flower to an open trumpet.

comparison_cards.title: Fruit-ridge tie-breaker
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Thin often translucent longitudinal ridges versus deeper grooves ending in small knobs on mature anthocarps.
comparison_cards.caution: Fruit lengths overlap 6–8 mm; do not use size alone.

comparison_cards.title: Acleisanthes versus four-o'clocks
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Check involucre bracts and fruit architecture; a long petaloid tube alone is not genus proof.
